# p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector_staged (Resource)

A staged AWS SSM (AI) connector. The connector is the `p0-connector-aws-ssm-ai` Lambda that P0 invokes to give AI agents SSH access to EC2 instances, one per AWS account. It reaches every instance that SSM manages in its account through SSM, and keeps each agent's SSH key in AWS Secrets Manager, in its own account.

Its role runs commands through the `AWS-RunShellScript` document, which runs them as root, so the connector can run any command as root on every SSM-managed instance in the account. Protect the Lambda and its role as you would root on those instances.

Staging records the connector in P0 before you deploy the Lambda. Then deploy the Lambda and its role, let P0's AWS IAM management role invoke the Lambda, and create a `p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector` resource with the same `id`, `region` and `vault` to complete the installation.

**Prerequisites:** P0 needs these integrations for the connector's AWS account. Staging fails until the first two are installed.

- AWS IAM management (see `p0_aws_iam_write`). P0 invokes the connector as its role.
- AWS OIDC (see `p0_aws_oidc_identity`). An agent's MCP server reads the agent's key through it.
- AWS Secrets Manager (see `p0_aws_secrets_manager`), which `vault` names. The connector keeps the keys there.

Destroying the connector also needs AWS IAM management and AWS OIDC, so keep them until it is gone. When one configuration holds them, add them to this resource's `depends_on`, so that Terraform destroys the connector first.

**Note:** This integration is in preview.

For the full install steps, see [AWS SSM MCP server](https://docs.p0.dev/integrations/resource-integrations/agentic-gateway/mcp-server/aws-ssm).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Requires P0's AWS IAM management (see p0_aws_iam_write) and AWS OIDC (see
# p0_aws_oidc_identity) for the connector's AWS account, and P0's AWS Secrets
# Manager integration for the same account (see p0_aws_secrets_manager). P0
# invokes the connector as AWS IAM management's role, and the connector keeps
# each agent's SSH key in that account's AWS Secrets Manager.

resource "p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector_staged" "example" {
  id     = "123456789012"
  region = "us-east-1"
  vault = {
    type           = "aws-sm"
    account_id     = "123456789012"
    secrets_region = "us-east-1"
  }

  # Destroying the connector needs AWS IAM management and AWS OIDC. If this
  # configuration installs them, depend on them, so that Terraform destroys
  # the connector first.
  # depends_on = [p0_aws_iam_write.example, p0_aws_oidc_identity.example]
}

# See the p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector example for the next steps (deploying the
# connector's Lambda and letting P0 invoke it) that complete the install.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The ID of the AWS account that the connector's Lambda runs in. P0 reaches every instance that SSM manages in this account through the connector.
- `region` (String) The AWS region that the connector's Lambda runs in. The connector runs only in commercial AWS regions.
- `vault` (Attributes) The secret manager where the connector keeps each agent's SSH key, as installed in P0. The connector writes each key, and the agent's MCP server reads it through AWS OIDC, only in the connector's own AWS account, so this must be that account's AWS Secrets Manager installation. Changing it replaces the connector. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vault))

### Read-Only

- `state` (String) This item's install progress in the P0 application:
	- 'stage': The item has been staged for installation
	- 'configure': The item is available to be added to P0, and may be configured
	- 'installed': The item is fully installed

<a id="nestedatt--vault"></a>
### Nested Schema for `vault`

Required:

- `account_id` (String) The ID of the AWS account whose AWS Secrets Manager installation in P0 (`p0_aws_secrets_manager`) keeps the keys. It must be the connector's `id`.
- `secrets_region` (String) The AWS region the connector keeps every key in, such as `us-west-2`. It must be a commercial AWS region. The connector's role may manage secrets in this region only.
- `type` (String) The secret manager. The only value is `aws-sm` (AWS Secrets Manager).
